summary: Iteration 55 tested three new features in Populus. Backend: 9/9 pytest cases PASS in /app/backend/tests/test_iter55_ai_summary_facts_terms.py (73.4s, XML at /app/test_reports/pytest/iter55_results.xml). (1) POST /api/feuds/{id}/ai-summary — with 5+5 argumentative comments and votes on both sides the Claude sonnet 4.6 endpoint returns the required shape {side_a[], side_b[], common[], party_a, party_b, generated_at, empty:false}; bullets are Italian strings ≤ 220 chars; empty-feud path returns empty:true with empty arrays; unauthenticated call → 401/403; unknown feud_id → 404. (2) Fact-checker: admin/generate-daily either produces new feuds carrying fact_check with decision in {PUBLISH,CORRECT} + reason, or (when dedupe blocks new generation) the retrospective validation confirms the 3 most recent AI feuds in DB all carry fact_check dicts with real Claude reasoning (all three decided CORRECT with detailed motivazioni). All required fields (title, party_a, party_b, summary) remain populated. (3) Terms: GET /api/legal/terms is public and returns {version:'v1', text (>1000 chars, contains Populus + Garante/GDPR), updated_at}; fresh user has terms_accepted:false; POST /api/users/me/accept-terms with {version:'v1'} → 200 and flips terms_accepted:true (persisted through /auth/me); wrong version → 400; unauthenticated → 401/403. Frontend (Expo web, mobile viewport 390x844): (T4) Loaded feud page as chat_a (already voted): BOTH stats-button and ai-summary-button appear in the vote area; tapping ai-summary-button opens ai-summary-modal with header 'SINTESI DEL PENSIERO' + subtitle 'Cosa sostiene ogni fazione, secondo l'IA'; on the tested feud (no comments yet) the modal correctly rendered the empty state 'Ancora troppi pochi commenti / Torna qui dopo un po' di discussione...'; ai-summary-refresh triggered a re-fetch; ai-summary-close dismissed the modal. (T5) After resetting terms_accepted_version=null for chat_a and injecting a valid token, the auto-redirect from / to /terms fired; header 'Prima di iniziare' + terms-scroll + terms-scroll-hint all rendered; terms-accept-btn had opacity 0.4 (disabled) before scroll; scrolling terms-scroll to bottom made the hint disappear and the button reach opacity 1.0; tapping terms-accept-btn persisted acceptance (auth/me confirmed terms_accepted:true, version:v1) and navigated away from /terms to /; terms-decline-btn is present as required. No React Native red screen. No deprecated Expo packages detected in package.json (no expo-av / expo-barcode-scanner / expo-background-fetch).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:2419 — _ai_faction_summary caps input to 25 comments per side and 250 chars each; this keeps token cost predictable but note the LLM often labels 2+2 comments per side as 'too scarce' and returns {empty:true} even though the feature docstring says '≥2 commenti'. If UX expectation is a real summary at ~2 comments/side, either loosen prompt rule 5 or set an internal threshold (e.g. return empty only when total<3) before hitting the LLM. Reproducible: with 2 short generic pro-A / pro-B comments the model returns empty; with 3+ concrete argumentative ones it returns real bullets.

server.py:2528 — reuse of get_comments(feud_id, user) via `# type: ignore` works but relies on the endpoint returning the same-side visibility contract; if that ever changes, the summary silently drifts. Consider extracting a shared _list_visible_comments() helper.

server.py:5235 — accept_legal_terms uses `Body(default_factory=dict)` and manual dict access instead of a Pydantic model; safe but breaks the pattern used elsewhere. A small `AcceptTermsBody(version: str)` would give consistent 422 validation errors.

server.py:3726 — _ai_fact_check_feud correctly swallows LLM errors and defaults to PUBLISH (safety net non-blocking). Verified in DB: 3/3 recently generated feuds carry fact_check, older 486 pre-feature feuds don't (as expected). Good defensive design.
terms.tsx:76 — refreshMe() is awaited after accept; the redirect happens via context update. Works cleanly, no race observed.

index.tsx:22 — redirect uses `user.terms_accepted === false` (strict); if backend ever omits the field (older tokens/undefined) the guard fails-open. Acceptable now because _public_user always emits the boolean, but worth guarding as `user.terms_accepted !== true` if you want fail-closed.
seed_data_creation: Created ~10 throwaway test users via /api/auth/signup + direct Mongo email_verified=True patch. Users voted+commented on the first feud to seed AI-summary material. For the frontend Terms flow, `chat_a@test.it` had `terms_accepted_version` unset in Mongo to simulate the fresh-user gate. Fact-checker validation used the 3 AI feuds generated during test run (feud_26308230760d, feud_465d06e46594, feud_185630ea4118) — all carry fact_check with real Claude reasoning.
context_for_next_testing_agent: AsyncStorage on Expo web writes token to localStorage under key `faide_token` as a JSON-encoded string (i.e. include the outer quotes). To bypass the disabled email login tab (AUTH_EMAIL_ENABLED=false in /app/frontend/app/auth.tsx), obtain a token from POST /api/auth/login and inject via `localStorage.setItem('faide_token', JSON.stringify(token))` before navigating. Pre-verified accounts chat_a/chat_b (test123) work. The AI faction-summary LLM (Claude sonnet 4.6) is strict about 'too scarce' — 2 short generic comments per side often trigger {empty:true}; use ≥3 concrete argumentative comments per side to force a real summary. Admin generate-daily may return created=[] if dedupe/freshness blocks new feuds; the test falls back to retrospective DB checks in that case. testIDs added this iteration: ai-summary-button, ai-summary-modal, ai-summary-refresh, ai-summary-close, ai-summary-side-a, ai-summary-side-b, terms-scroll, terms-scroll-hint, terms-accept-btn, terms-decline-btn, terms-error.
rca_of_issue: N/A — all tests pass. One transient during test authoring: the AI ai-summary endpoint returned {empty:true} on 2+2 short comments because Claude's prompt (rule 5: 'commenti troppo scarni per un'analisi') deems minimal input insufficient; fixed by seeding 3 concrete argumentative comments per side. Documented as a soft-UX concern in critical_code_review_comments — not a bug.
